publisher: U.S. House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party
title: Moolenaar: American Companies & Governments Should Cut Ties With New Pentagon-Listed Chinese Military Companies
key_claim: On 8 June 2026 the Pentagon added WuXi AppTec (and other firms) to its Section 1260H list of 'Chinese military companies'; congressional leaders urged U.S. firms and governments to cut ties and remove their products from supply chains, citing the BIOSECURE Act signed into law in December.
notes: Tier 1 government (legislative-branch) source. Anchors the decoupling/national-security side of the collision.

publisher: National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology (NSCEB), U.S. Senate
title: NSCEB Applauds ITC Investigation into Unfair Chinese Economic Practices to Distort the Biotechnology Market
key_claim: The U.S. International Trade Commission opened a new investigation, mandated in the FY2026 appropriations report on an NSCEB recommendation, into Chinese-government practices that unfairly support Chinese biotechnology firms and undermine the competitiveness of American firms.
notes: Tier 1 legislative-branch source, used as the single structural anchor (3-6 month band). Establishes the policy/national-security framing.

publisher: IQVIA Institute for Human Data Science
title: Global R&D Trends 2026
date_evidence: Global R&D Trends 2026 | IQVIA ... The report was published on March 25, 2026 ... products from China-headquartered companies now represent 12% of the early-stage pipeline, up from 2% a decade ago
key_claim: Products from China-headquartered companies now represent about 12% of the global early-stage pipeline, up from roughly 2% a decade ago, and deals between China-headquartered and international companies reached an all-time high.
notes: Tier 2 institute/data-provider report. Provides the consensus-reframing quantification on innovation origin.

title: China Dominates Big Licensing Deals as M&A Starts 2026 With a Bang
key_claim: DealForma data show China leading large biopharma licensing deals in early 2026, with deal volume cooling slightly but bigger payouts keeping licensing and M&A activity hot, extending 2025's record.
notes: Tier 2 specialist deal-database provider. Directional confirmation of China's dominance in large licensing.

title: China poised to eclipse US innovators with surge in global licensing
key_claim: An INTERPHEX 2026 panel reported that nearly 40% of global pharma licensing originated from Chinese innovation, that China's clinical-trial activity is now 'on par with' the U.S., and that WuXi AppTec posted record 2025 revenue with U.S. sales up more than 34% year over year, pointing to a 'bifurcated global ecosystem'.
verbatim_quote: Nearly 40% of global pharma licensing originated from Chinese innovation
notes: Tier 3 trade press reporting an industry panel and GlobalData; carries the headline licensing-origination share and the bifurcation framing.

title: As Chinese biotechs recognize their value, the bargain era may be over
key_claim: China cross-border licensing reached a record estimated $137.7 billion in 2025; the average upfront payment rose from $102 million to $141 million between 2024 and 2025 (Evaluate data), and an analyst notes 'such a high proportion of the pipeline is now China-derived' that sourcing from China is 'almost an inevitability' in areas like oncology, even as rising prices end the bargain era and many Chinese firms still lack late-stage development experience.
verbatim_quote: Such a high proportion of the pipeline is now China-derived, so going to China is almost an inevitability in some areas, like oncology
notes: Tier 3 trade press citing Evaluate data; supplies deal-value anchors and the counter-argument (prices rising, late-stage capability gap).

title: Bristol Myers Squibb turns to China's Hengrui to replenish pipeline
key_claim: Bristol Myers Squibb turned to China's Jiangsu Hengrui to replenish its drug pipeline, licensing a HER3-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, illustrating big pharma's use of China-originated assets to offset patent-cliff losses.
notes: Tier 3 business journalism; concrete megadeal example of pipeline replenishment via a China-originated molecule.
